title: Partner Health & Executive Bridge: QBR Deck Templates (Standard + Enterprise)
content:
Purpose: A compact, reusable QBR deck structure that combines a customer health checklist with an "Executive Bridge" narrative designed to align product usage to executive business goals, and a renewal playbook with risk-tiered actions. Two variants provided: Standard (customer-facing, 20–30 minute meeting) and Enterprise (extended, 45–60 minute, technical appendix).

How to use this file: Copy slide titles and speaker notes into your slide tool. Use the renewal tracker table below as the canonical checklist to paste into spreadsheets. Replace all <PLACEHOLDER> markers with real metrics.

1) Executive Summary (single-slide)
- Slide title: "Where we are and why we met"
- Speaker notes: 60–90 seconds. One-sentence customer health label (Green/Yellow/Red), short ARR/usage trend bullet, top 2 asks for this quarter. Call out renewal window if within 90 days.

2) One-page Impact Story (Standard + Enterprise)
- Slide title: "Business outcomes enabled"
- Speaker notes: Use metric pairs: outcome (e.g., "Faster time-to-insight") + supporting metric ("50% faster report generation; API latency 99p reduced from 420ms to 120ms"). Include a customer quote or NPS snippet if available.

3) Usage & Health Snapshot (Standard) / Deep Usage Map (Enterprise)
- Standard slide content: MAU, active seats, API tokens/month, avg tokens per call, spend vs. budget, 30/60/90-day trend sparklines.
- Enterprise appendix: feature-level adoption (embeddings, rerank, streaming), KV cache hit-rate, cold-start ratio, peak QPS by route, 95/99 latency by model.

4) Reliability & Incidents
- What to present: # incidents since last QBR, P0/P1 summaries, MTTR improvements, outstanding action items.
- Enterprise addendum: list incident postmortem links, mitigations deployed, open SRE tickets.

5) Cost & Efficiency (Playbook entry)
- Show unit economics: cost per 1M tokens, net ARR impact. Recommend immediate optimizations (batching, prefix cache, smaller model on lower-critical paths).

6) Product Roadmap Alignment (Executive Bridge)
- One slide mapping Redwoods' near-term roadmap items to the customer's priorities. Use 3 columns: Customer priority, Redwood initiative, Impact/ETA.
- Speaker notes: Frame roadmap items as mitigations for customer risks and accelerators for planned outcomes.

7) Risks & Dependencies (Renewal focus)
- Template: Risk description, severity (L/M/H), potential ARR impact, mitigation owner, ETA.
- Speaker notes: Prioritize top 3 risks and proposed mitigations in the meeting.

8) Renewal & Expansion Playbook (core of this doc)
- Three-tier risk model: Green (low risk), Yellow (moderate), Red (high). For each tier provide proactive plays, timeline, and escalation path.
  * Green: Execute NPS check-in + expansion motion. Owner: CSM. Timeline: 30 days. Play: propose pilot for new route; offer usage credits for low-friction trial.
  * Yellow: Tactical remediation + exec check. Owner: Senior CSM + Solutions Eng. Timeline: 14–30 days. Play: focused runbook (billing review, latency tune, dedicated capacity trial).
  * Red: Renewal intervention. Owner: Head of CS + Account Exec + Engineering SLA review. Timeline: immediate (7–14 days). Play: on-call SRE deep-dive, temporary credits, formal exec alignment.

9) Tactical Renewal Tracker (paste into spreadsheet)
- Columns: Owner | Action | Due date | Status | Notes | Jira/PM link
- Sample rows (replace <>):
  - Diego Alvarez | Run prefix-cache audit, propose config | 2026-03-01 | in_progress | initial audit shows 18% hit-rate | JIRA-8123
  - Maya Chen | Exec alignment call w/ VP Product | 2026-02-22 | scheduled | propose enterprise pilot | SL: #cs-execs thread
  - Samir Patel | Billing anomaly reconciliation | 2026-02-28 | done | credits issued for spike | BILL-443

10) Ask & Next Steps (closing slide)
- Default asks: commit to 1 pilot, identify exec sponsor, agree on renewal cadence.
- Speaker notes: confirm decision owners and calendarize follow-ups (owner + date).

Enterprise Appendix (technical + legal) – only include when meeting includes engineering or procurement
- Slide: "Security & Compliance posture" – list certifications, KMS integration status, audit log availability, data residency, any open compliance items.
- Slide: "Throughput & Cost Profile" – per-route capacity sizing, recommended Dedicated config, burst policy.
- Slide: "SLA and Escrow" – if requested, show SLA packages, lead time for Dedicated, and support tiers.

Health Checklist (one-page quick audit)
- Contract & Renewal: renewal date, notice period, CSM assigned, AM assigned, auto-renew?
- Usage: 30/60/90 day delta, key routes, replays of failed calls percentage, cost anomalies
- Experience: major incidents > P2, ongoing bugs open >14 days
- Commercial: discount tiers in place, pending legal redlines, PO received?
- Security/Compliance: latest SOC/ISO attestations, outstanding info requests

Meeting Facilitation Tips
- Start with the impact story and the single-line health label. Keep slides to visuals + 1–2 talking bullets.
- Don’t overload with raw logs—especially for execs. Move those details to the Enterprise appendix or a follow-up tech working session.
- Use the Executive Bridge to translate technical improvement into business outcomes: e.g., "Reducing 99p latency by 300ms reduces customer churn risk for core workflows by X% (cite case study)."

Sample Renewal Playbook Scenarios (unique examples)
- Scenario A (usage plateau, churn risk): run a 6-week expansion pilot on an underused route, attach success KPIs (20% lift in tokens/month), assign product adoption mentor, tie to 6-month discount.
- Scenario B (cost shock after feature rollout): propose temporary credits + config changes (quantization + batching), real-time cost alert dashboard, 2-week post-change review.
- Scenario C (security procurement delay): provide audit artifacts bundle, assign legal point-of-contact, propose interim contract amendment for data residency.

Append: Quick copy/paste slide checklist (20-slide compact deck):
1 Cover: customer + date + health label
2 Executive summary (one-line)
3 Impact story
4 Top metrics snapshot
5 Reliability incidents
6 Cost overview
7 Feature adoption map
8 Roadmap alignment
9 Risk heatmap
10 Renewal ask
11 Expansion opportunities
12 Commercial summary (ARR, pipeline)
13 Support and SRE items
14 Security/compliance summary (enterprise only)
15 Deployment recommendations (dedicated/private)
16 Experiment plan (15–30 day pilots)
17 Success criteria + KPIs
18 Action owner list / tracker
19 Appendix links (postmortems, billing, legal)
20 Thank you / next steps

Notes on tone and customization
- Standard decks: concise, outcomes-forward, use customer language.
- Enterprise decks: pragmatic, show evidence, include mitigation timelines and technical appendices.

Version history & suggested chores before sending
- v0.1 (2025-11-04): initial template and checklist (Maya Chen)
- v0.2 (2026-01-12): added enterprise appendix and incident runbook (Diego Alvarez)
- v0.3 (2026-02-15): updated renewal tracker samples and playbook scenarios (Samir Patel)

Copyable resources (placeholders)
- Placeholder KPI block: "<MAU>, <API calls/mo>, <avg tokens/call>, <ARR>, <renewal date>"
- Meeting invite template: short subject line ("QBR — <Customer> — <MM/DD> | 30m") and agenda bullets (impact, metrics, asks)
- Slack template for pre-meeting alignment: "Heads-up: QBR scheduled <date>. Please review incident list: <link>. Need SRE on-call? Y/N."

Open questions to resolve in preparation
- Has engineering completed the prefix-cache audit? (owner: Diego)
- Legal sign-off on the proposed amendment for data residency? (owner: Priya)
- Which exec will represent the customer on the renewal decision? (owner: CSM)

End of document.

Attachments suggested (links to paste into the slide footer):
- Billing reconciliation sheet: <spreadsheet link>
- Live incident tracker: <sre-pagerduty-link>
- Roadmap entry: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRD/Serving+Runtime+Roadmap
